subject: Art & Design
title: Stanley Kubrick: Obsessive Perfectionist
description: A micro-lesson that makes Stanley Kubrick: Obsessive Perfectionist usable.

hook.text: Kubrick made Shelley Duvall film the baseball bat scene in The Shining 127 times. Take after take after take.

buildup.text: Stanley Kubrick controlled every detail: lighting, set design, music, lenses, even the color of props.

discovery.text: His symmetrical compositions and one-point perspective shots create beauty that feels unsettling.

twist.text: He genre-hopped: war (Full Metal Jacket), sci-fi (2001), horror (The Shining), period drama (Barry Lyndon).

climax.text: Barry Lyndon was lit entirely by candlelight using a NASA lens. No other filmmaker would attempt it.

punchline.text: Kubrick didn't make films for his time. He made them for all time.

quiz.question: What lens did Kubrick use to film Barry Lyndon by candlelight?
options: A special NASA lens designed for satellite photography
A standard cinema lens with high ISO film
A custom German lens made for submarines

details.summary: Stanley Kubrick's legendary perfectionism produced some of cinema's most visually stunning and intellectually challenging films. From '2001: A Space Odyssey' to 'The Shining,' his obsessive control over every detail — demanding hundreds of takes and inventing new techniques — created an unmatched.
details.whyItMatters: Kubrick proved that cinema could be both commercially successful and intellectually rigorous. His obsessive attention to detail set a standard that continues to influence directors who aspire to treat film as a total art form.
takeaways: Kubrick's perfectionism produced cinema's most stunning films
He demanded hundreds of takes and invented new techniques
His work proved commercial success and art could coexist

faq.question: Why is 2001: A Space Odyssey considered groundbreaking?
faq.answer: Released in 1968, its special effects remained unmatched until Star Wars. Kubrick used practical effects — rotating sets, front-projection — to create convincing space travel.

faq.question: Was Kubrick really as obsessive as legend suggests?
faq.answer: Largely yes. He famously demanded 127 takes of a single scene in 'The Shining' and had doors opened and closed 70 times to get the sound right. He controlled every aspect of his films including marketing, poster design, and theater projection specifications.
